subject: Segmented rate architecture: seat vs consumption split and rollback protections
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clearglass.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearglass.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-26T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial options for segmented pricing and rollback guardrails

Hi Naomi / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood's runtime but the finance team pushed back on a single blended rate for the whole platform. Their ask: a clearer seat vs consumption split (fixed base for seats and predictable per-token/embedding tiers after thresholds) and a defined rollback / exit protection if the migration materially underperforms (we have internal SLAs to hit in 60–90 days).

Two quick asks to start:
- Can you sketch a simple segmented-rate construct (seat floor + consumption overlay + volume step-downs) and show an example with our Q4 profile (peak inference + steady embeddings)?
- Can you outline a non-standard sideletter that preserves runtime licensing for our custom model artifacts (we want a carveout so our license isn’t hostage if we change vendors) and a short rollback credit (not full refund, but something to offset migration cost)?

We can share our usage snapshot if that helps — attaching the basic billing extract.

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Cloudops, ClearGlass Analytics
Sam.Patel@clearglass.io

Attachment: clearglass-billing-snapshot-q2.csv (csv)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clearglass.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for segmented pricing and rollback guardrails

Sam — thanks for the clear asks. Appreciate the billing snapshot, that helps.

High-level options I want to propose for quick review (I'll put numbers in the attached spreadsheet):
1) Seat-floor + consumption overlay (recommended for teams with steady control-plane usage)
   - Fixed monthly seat fee covers X inference instances and baseline support;
   - Consumption band A (0–5M tokens): $0.00XX/token (higher); band B (5–25M): $0.00YY/token; band C: negotiated;
2) Consumption-first (for heavy token customers)
   - Lower per-token but higher variability — includes optional reserved burst pool for peak events;
3) Hybrid (segmented): minimum seat commitment to guarantee latency + consumption-tiered discounts — this is what I expect will map to your ask about predictability.

Rollback / exit protection concept:
- 90-day migration window; if latency or throughput misses agreed SLOs (detailed in a pilot SLA), we provide a migration credit equal to N months of committed seats capped at M% of first-year ARR.
- Sideletter: carveout language around runtime-resident customer model artifacts — Redwood will not assert runtime license restrictions for custom models you bring; we can offer an escrowed runtime artifact for business continuity on export.

Two asks from our side to make numbers specific:
- Confirm whether you prefer seat-count commitments (seats) or deduced baseline GPU-hours (we can translate);
- Confirm target rollback protection ceiling (e.g., 10% of first-year committed spend vs 20%).

I've attached a segmented-rate workbook and a short draft of the rollback sideletter. Connor / Jordan — looping you for technical read / legal framing.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: segmented-rate-proposal-v2.xlsx, draft-sideletter-rollback.docx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-26T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for segmented pricing and rollback guardrails

On 2026-07-26 11:03, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Rollback / exit protection concept:
> - 90-day migration window; if latency or throughput misses agreed SLOs (detailed in a pilot SLA), we provide a migration credit equal to N months of committed seats capped at M% of first-year ARR.

Quick technical/commercial notes from infra side — adding a slightly different option that may be easier to operationalize and less risky for Redwood while still addressing ClearGlass's ask: a segmented-rate architecture with an "integration tranche". Outline below: 

- Tranche A (Platform-resilience tranche): small seat minimum to guarantee latency and KV cache prefills (this ensures deterministic cold-starts for your workload).
- Tranche B (Consumption overlay): per-token bands as Naomi outlined. Consumption priced slightly lower for calls that hit the KV cache > 40% (we can instrument and report this).
- Tranche C (Canary pilot bucket): a short pre-production bucket with discounted tokens for the first 30 days of go-live; if pilot signals meet success criteria (P95 latency < X ms and model correctness thresholds), remaining committed seats convert; otherwise the rollback credit is applied to offset migration & integration labor (we recommend a 3-month cap).

Runtime license carveout (practical wording suggestion):
- Redwood grants a limited runtime sublicense for exported customer models for the purpose of returning artifacts should the customer exercise rollback within the audit window. This is tightly scoped: no onward commercial distribution, and we log accesses to provide an audit trail.

Operational tradeoffs to flag:
- Pros: predictable economics, explicit data to prove canary success, minimizes overcommit for customer.
- Cons: increased billing complexity and more bookkeeping in the console for tranche conversions; slightly larger legal sideletter.

If legal/finance want a conservative starting point, we can structure: 6-month pilot credit (discounted tokens), then a 12-month seat commitment with conversion triggers. Numbers in the attached workbook.

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: interop-risk-matrix.pdf
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clearglass.io>

Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearglass.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Commercial options for segmented pricing and rollback guardrails

Thanks — this is helpful and the tranche/canary idea seems practical. A few quick confirmations before we loop procurement/legal: 
- Please populate the spreadsheet with two scenarios: (A) conservative: 3-month pilot credit + 12-month seat commitment at X; (B) aggressive: 30-day canary + 6-month conversion + lower band rates.
- Define the exact trigger metrics for canary success (we need explicit P95, error-rate, and model-quality thresholds).
- For the runtime carveout, our counsel will want the exact export mechanism and escrow configuration; can you add a short appendix describing the export format and access controls?

If you can get updated numbers + the short appendix by EOD Friday we’ll have our procurement and legal review over the following week and aim to sign a sideletter before month-end.

Sam
--
Sam Patel
Head of Cloudops, ClearGlass Analytics
